quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Open the mouth about halfway: one finger-width. 'Pen' should not need a wide jaw.
quests.explanation: The jaw is half open and the tongue mid-front. A wider mouth would turn 'pen' into 'pan'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /e/ has the jaw half open and the tongue mid-front; /æ/ needs the jaw dropped clearly lower, tongue low and forward, mouth wide.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Drop your jaw further than feels natural and stretch the corners of the mouth. That is how 'cat' feels.
quests.explanation: Low, forward tongue and a wide mouth. A narrower mouth would drift towards the vowel of 'pet'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Check the mouth opening: roughly one finger-width for /e/, closer to two stacked fingers for /æ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The nasal /n/ tempts learners to open wider. Keep the jaw half open.
quests.explanation: The jaw stays moderate. Opening wider would give 'tan'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /æ/ is longer and more spread than /e/. Learners often use /e/ for both, so exaggerate the jaw drop at first.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: 'Man' and 'men' differ only by jaw drop. For 'man', go low.
quests.explanation: The mouth opens wide, and the vowel lengthens a little before /n/ while keeping its low front quality.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Tongue height is the cue: it falls from mid-front /e/ to low-front /æ/. Lips are slightly spread for both.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Feel the jaw: half closed for 'bed', not dropped as in 'bad'.
quests.explanation: Mid-front tongue and a modest jaw drop. Drop the jaw further and it becomes 'bad'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Spread the lips slightly for both, but let the jaw do the work: /e/ stops about halfway, /æ/ keeps going.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The final /k/ closes the word fast, but the vowel before it needs a wide jaw.
quests.explanation: A wide mouth that is easier to see in a mirror than to hear. Check your jaw as you say it.
quests.vowelTensionRule: If a word with /æ/ is coming out as /e/, check that the front of the tongue is low, not hovering at mid-height.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The letters ea usually say 'ee', but not here. Think of 'bed' with an h.
quests.explanation: Ea usually spells the long vowel, but 'head', 'dead' and 'breath' break the rule.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Before nasals and voiced stops /æ/ tends to lengthen while /e/ stays brief, but the jaw gap is still the deciding cue.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: A nasal cluster /nd/ follows. The vowel before it is low and wide.
quests.explanation: The /nd/ ending changes nothing. It is the same wide vowel as in 'cat'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /e/ and /æ/ differ by about one step of tongue height on the vowel chart: mid-front versus near-open front.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Same ea spelling trap as before. Listen for the half-open vowel after /br/.
quests.explanation: The /br/ cluster makes the vowel feel shorter, but the jaw still stays half open.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Spelling won't tell you: a gives /e/ in 'many' and /æ/ in 'cat', and ea gives /e/ in 'head'. Decide with ears and jaw.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Voiced /g/ makes the vowel feel longer. Keep the jaw wide, then close with /g/.
quests.explanation: Voiced /g/ stretches the vowel slightly, but its quality stays wide. Don't let the extra length push you towards the other vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The contrast is clearest in stressed syllables; in weak syllables both tend to drift towards a neutral vowel.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The ai spelling normally says 'ay'. This word is a famous exception.
quests.explanation: Ai normally says 'ay', but 'said' is an irregular spelling that rhymes with 'bed'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: A self-check: rest a hand under your chin. The jaw should drop noticeably further for /æ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The /bl/ cluster tempts you to hurry the vowel. Slow down and drop the jaw.
quests.explanation: After the cluster the jaw drops wide, and then /k/ shuts it.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are short, so the only question is how high the front of the tongue rises.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The ie spelling is another trap. 'Friend' rhymes with 'send'.
quests.explanation: The i is silent. Say 'frend' and the vowel lands in the right place.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /e/ has the jaw half open and the tongue mid-front; /æ/ needs the jaw dropped clearly lower, tongue low and forward, mouth wide.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Imagine biting into one: the jaw drops wide to start the word.
quests.explanation: The stressed first syllable begins wide open. The final -le is a syllabic /l/, not a vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Check the mouth opening: roughly one finger-width for /e/, closer to two stacked fingers for /æ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Back to rounding: lips pushed forward, vowel held before the dark /l/.
quests.explanation: Lips rounded, vowel held: the same contrast as 'full' versus 'fool' that you practised earlier.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In a mirror, /uː/ shows a tight forward pout and /ʊ/ a gentle, relaxed circle.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The a spelling lies. 'Many' starts with the same vowel as 'men'.
quests.explanation: The a is pronounced like an e, a historical oddity. 'Any' behaves the same way.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /æ/ is longer and more spread than /e/. Learners often use /e/ for both, so exaggerate the jaw drop at first.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Hear it as 'hap-ee'. The first syllable is wide, the second is just a light /i/.
quests.explanation: The stressed first syllable is wide. The final vowel is only a light, weak /i/.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Tongue height is the cue: it falls from mid-front /e/ to low-front /æ/. Lips are slightly spread for both.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Both vowels in 'finish' are short and loose. No smile required.
quests.explanation: Both vowels are short and lax. If you smile, you have said 'feenish'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɪ/ is lax and slightly lowered; /iː/ is higher and tenser with spread lips. Quality carries the contrast, and length only reinforces it.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The ea strikes again. Say it aloud: the first vowel sounds like 'wet'.
quests.explanation: Another ea spelling with the short vowel. 'Whether' sounds identical in RP, so the ear alone cannot tell them apart.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Spread the lips slightly for both, but let the jaw do the work: /e/ stops about halfway, /æ/ keeps going.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Ignore the weak syllables that follow and drop the jaw wide on the first.
quests.explanation: The strong syllable is the first one. The weak syllables after it are not part of this contrast.
quests.vowelTensionRule: If a word with /æ/ is coming out as /e/, check that the front of the tongue is low, not hovering at mid-height.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Two vowels, the first strong. The strong one is half open.
quests.explanation: Ea spells this vowel in 'ready', 'steady' and 'instead'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Before nasals and voiced stops /æ/ tends to lengthen while /e/ stays brief, but the jaw gap is still the deciding cue.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Two syllables, the first stressed. Half-open jaw, then a quick weak ending.
quests.explanation: A short half-open vowel in the stressed first syllable. The -age ending is weak.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /e/ and /æ/ differ by about one step of tongue height on the vowel chart: mid-front versus near-open front.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Three syllables; the first carries the stress. Wide jaw there.
quests.explanation: Although 'pass' alone takes the long open vowel in RP, 'passenger' keeps the short wide one.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Spelling won't tell you: a gives /e/ in 'many' and /æ/ in 'cat', and ea gives /e/ in 'head'. Decide with ears and jaw.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The -gu- is a /gw/ sound, so the vowel sits before the nasal /ŋ/. Keep the jaw wide.
quests.explanation: The nasal /ŋ/ colours the vowel slightly, but the jaw still drops wide.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The contrast is clearest in stressed syllables; in weak syllables both tend to drift towards a neutral vowel.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Two syllables, strong then weak. The strong one is half open.
quests.explanation: Stress falls on le-, with the short half-open vowel. The second syllable is weak.
quests.vowelTensionRule: A self-check: rest a hand under your chin. The jaw should drop noticeably further for /æ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Strong, weak, weak: drop the jaw on the first vowel and let the other two shrink.
quests.explanation: In casual speech it sounds like 'cam-ra', but the strong first vowel is unchanged.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are short, so the only question is how high the front of the tongue rises.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: The stressed syllable is the first. The 'di' that follows is short and weak.
quests.explanation: Stress sits on the first syllable. The weak /ɪ/ in 'di' must not steal it.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /e/ has the jaw half open and the tongue mid-front; /æ/ needs the jaw dropped clearly lower, tongue low and forward, mouth wide.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Four syllables, but only the first is strong. Half-open mouth.
quests.explanation: Only the first of the four syllables is strong. Don't let the weak ones pull the stress away.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Check the mouth opening: roughly one finger-width for /e/, closer to two stacked fingers for /æ/.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Strong first syllable, then a syllabic /l/. Open wide for the vowel.
quests.explanation: The /tr/ cluster does not change the vowel; the jaw simply drops after it.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /æ/ is longer and more spread than /e/. Learners often use /e/ for both, so exaggerate the jaw drop at first.

quests.instruction: SLIDE OR TAP TO MATCH THE TARGET VOWEL SOUND
quests.hint: Lips pushed forward and held, then /l/.
quests.explanation: Long and rounded, like the vowel in 'true' and 'soup'.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Short oo words (book, good, foot) take /ʊ/, long ones (food, moon) take /uː/. No spelling rule separates them, so group them by sound.
